question.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=12\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & -16 \\ -16 & 29\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}29 & 16 \\ 16 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
